attempts.raw: {"patches": [{"section": "cash", "original": "The $0.3 billion decline in operating cash flow from FY2024 came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6].", "type": "cause", "text": "Operating cash flow fell to $19.8 billion in FY2025 from $20.1 billion in FY2024 on lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [F59][F58][P6]."}]}

sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 jump came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized prices across all products, and net income has declined every year since, to $8.0 billion in FY2025 [F8][D274][P47][F20][D343].
Note that the table's revenue is a later recast, not the figure first reported: FY2025 is $51.8 billion here against $58.9 billion in that year's 10-K [F10][X10][R1].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.7pp of the 4.9% growth, while non-U.S. added 2.0pp [D382][D384][D342][D400].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in FY2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but grew only 0.1%, while natural gas liquids grew 28.2% and contributed 1.5pp [D551][D552][D665][D666].
Net income fell 13.6% against revenue growth of 4.9%, so there was no operating leverage in FY2025 [D343][D342].
Diluted EPS fell 18.7% while net income fell 13.6%, because the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D345][D343][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025, with D&A at 19.5% of revenue and cost of revenue at 37.9% [D351][D330][D326].
DD&A rose $1.9 billion in FY2025 mainly on the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
SG&A fell $265 million on the absence of $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses, partly offset by restructuring severance [P23].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9%, above the 32.4% of FY2024, widening the gap between pre-tax and net income [D332][D298].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 1.52x of FY2022 [F59][F20][D333][D226].
Operating cash flow fell to $19.8 billion in FY2025 from $20.1 billion in FY2024 on lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [F59][F58][P6].
Operating cash flow was 33.6% of revenue, and capex of $10.2 billion in FY2022 was 1.35x D&A [D331][F66][D228].
Free cash flow is only disclosed through FY2022, when it was $18.2 billion, so later conversion cannot be measured from the pack [F73].
Net cash was $7.1 billion, or 12.1% of revenue, in the 100th percentile against six energy peers whose median was -7.7% [D337][D338][D850][D851].
In FY2025 the company spent $12.6 billion on capital, $5.0 billion on buybacks, $4.0 billion on dividends and $0.9 billion retiring debt, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the stated 30% framework [D339][F59][P31].
Return on average equity fell to 12.4%, below the 14.9% peer median and in the 33rd percentile [D341][D853][D852].
The revenue basis break is the main data-quality flag: every year in the table differs from the first-reported figure, so growth and margins mix two presentations [R1][F10][X10].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 and net income has fallen 41.3%, 15.6% and 13.6% in the three years since [D274][D275][D309][D343].
The diluted share count rose 6.1% in FY2025, reversing prior shrinkage, which amplified the EPS decline [D356][D345].
Segment revenue members sum to 227% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so segment shares cannot be added together [R4].
Net margin: a print below the 15.4% of FY2025 would extend the three-year decline, while a return above the 17.9% median would break it [F30][D831].
Diluted share count: a further rise above the 1,253.4 million of FY2025 would confirm dilution; a fall back toward the 1,180.9 million of FY2024 would reverse it [X131][X130].
Net cash: a drop below the $7.1 billion of FY2025 would signal the buyback and disposition programme is outrunning cash generation [D337].
